text:
elaine_support: NovumBio on Private deployment (vpc-0a1b2c) reporting intermittent 502/503 from their app -> our private API endpoint since ~08:30 UTC. They also see TLS handshake errors in their sidecar logs. We changed tunnel MTU on the peer yesterday. Anyone able to jump on the peering side?

raj_ops: I'm on call, digging in. Can you paste the exact repro steps + sample curl/dig output from the customer?

elaine_support: Repro from their env: 
1) curl -v https://private-api.redwood.internal/health
2) dig @10.0.2.2 private-api.redwood.internal +short

Customer output: 
```
$ curl -v https://private-api.redwood.internal/health
* Rebuilt URL to: https://private-api.redwood.internal/health/
* Trying 10.1.5.12...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to 10.1.5.12 (10.1.5.12) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering http/1.1
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert certificate unknown
* SSL: certificate verify failed
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) SSL: certificate verify failed
```

And DNS failing intermittently: `dig @10.0.2.2 private-api.redwood.internal +short` returns nothing ~1/4 attempts.

mike_net: Can you run `sudo ipsec statusall` on our customer-edge peer and paste any BGP status? Also I want `show ip route`/`bgp summary` from the DX/VRF.

elaine_support: customer shared an ipsec excerpt: 
```
ikev2-spd0: up, 2 flows
conn novum-vpn: IKE SA established between 3.4.5.6[4500] and 10.20.30.40[4500]
child sa novum-vpn-esp: INSTALLED, reqid=1 in=10.1.0.0/16 out=10.20.0.0/16
```
No obvious rekeys.

sarah_serving: Our app logs show a bunch of 502s at the same time, with upstream error: `tls: remote error: tls: bad certificate` coming from 10.1.5.12:443 (the private-api host).

nathan_security: Two quick hypotheses: 1) DNS requests from customer are being NAT'd to a different resolver (asymmetric path) causing inconsistent answers/EDNS issues. 2) Their firewall/HA cluster started SNATting outbound connections to an ephemeral IP which isn't in our peering egress allowlist, so replies may be sent to the wrong address/VRF and TLS handshake can fail if SNI or cert routing depends on client IP. Ask them if they recently changed HA pair or firewall firmware.

raj_ops: Good call. Elaine, did they mention any recent firewall change?

elaine_support: They said they rolled a new HA firewall pair earlier today and toggled 'preserve source' to off (so SNAT enabled).

mike_net: That matches observed tcpdump from our edge (ran a quick capture): 
```
sudo tcpdump -nni eth2 host 10.1.5.12 and port 53 -c 20
12:03:41.123456 IP 192.0.2.101.33445 > 10.0.2.2.53: 12345+ A? private-api.redwood.internal. (47)
12:03:41.223556 IP 198.51.100.12.33445 > 10.0.2.2.53: 12345+ A? private-api.redwood.internal. (47)
```
We see two different source IPs for DNS queries (192.0.2.101 and 198.51.100.12) from the same customer subnet. Looks like SNATing across HA nodes.

nathan_security: If the source IP changes, and the egress allowlist only permits 192.0.2.101, replies that go to 198.51.100.12 might be dropped or routed to a different path. That can break handshake timing and DNS caching, causing intermittent 502/handshake errors.

raj_ops: Action items: 
- Elaine: ask customer to disable outbound SNAT/preserve client IP (or configure static SNAT IPs that match our allowlist) on their firewall HA pair.
- Mike: check our peering ACLs for the NovumBio VRF and confirm allowed source IPs.
- Nathan: check TLS termination logs for any SNI mismatch traces tied to client IP.

elaine_support: Reached out to customer in same thread. They flipped preserve-source back on and configured static SNAT IPs (198.51.100.12 -> replaced with 192.0.2.101). They said they can test now.

(5 minutes later)

elaine_support: Customer reports tests look clean: curl -v now returns 200 and dig returns a consistent A.
```
$ curl -v https://private-api.redwood.internal/health
* Connected to 10.1.5.12 (10.1.5.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake completed
* HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```

mike_net: I confirmed from edge tcpdump we now only see 192.0.2.101 as source for DNS and app traffic; no more 198.51.100.12.

nathan_security: Great — root cause: firewall HA SNATed outbound to multiple ephemeral addresses, causing asymmetric flow and allowed-source mismatch with our peering egress policy. Workaround: use preserve-source or static SNAT IPs that are in the allowlist.

elaine_support: Marking as resolved with workaround; will follow up with KB article for customers running HA firewall pairs.

infra-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-4493 — NovumBio private peering: transient DNS/TLS failures due to customer SNAT. Assigned to raj_ops.

elaine_support: Thanks all. Adding remediation checklist: update onboarding checklist to ask customers to supply firewall SNAT behavior and static egress IPs before private provisioning.

raj_ops: Agree, will update playbook.
